project_context.name: Stepped Wave Animation for LSP Progress in Heirline Statusline
project_context.description: Implement fast, continuous left-to-right traveling wave animation using Unicode stepped pattern (⎯⎺) for LSP progress state in NixieProgressBar component

user_requirements.continuity: Continuous left-to-right travel, no rest periods

validation_criteria: Characters render without boxes or missing glyphs

nodes.description: Design wave pattern array with 9 frames and validate visual progression
deliverables: Lua table with 9 wave pattern strings (8 chars each)
Visual representation of all frames in sequence

Pattern logic: plateau builds (3 frames) then travels right (6 frames)
validation_criteria: Each frame is exactly 8 characters (fits ┣┫ brackets)
Pattern shows clear wave progression
Loop from frame 9 back to frame 1 is seamless
Peak (⎺⎺⎺) moves right by 1 position each frame after building

metadata.algorithm: Build 3-char peak left-to-right, then travel entire wave across, loop

nodes.description: Design frame calculation logic for 150ms timing with modulo 9
deliverables: Lua code snippet for frame calculation: math.floor((vim.loop.now() or 0) / 150) % 9
Explanation of why 150ms timing creates fast animation
Comparison with current 200ms timing
Total animation cycle time: 9 frames × 150ms = 1.35 seconds
validation_criteria: Frame calculation produces integers 0-8
Timing aligns with 150ms per frame requirement
Works with existing vim.loop.now() approach
No floating point precision issues

nodes.description: Design implementation strategy to isolate wave animation to LSP state only
deliverables: Architectural decision: Add self.wave_pattern field vs separate provider logic
Implementation approach: Conditional in provider function
Strategy to preserve existing states (IDLE, MODIFIED, SEARCH, DIAGNOSTIC)
Testing approach to ensure no regression
validation_criteria: Wave animation only affects LSP_PROGRESS state
Other states continue using block-based display (▓░)
No changes to colors, labels, or brackets for LSP state
Minimal code changes (follow user preference for clean code)

metadata.implementation_approach: Add conditional in provider function: if self.state == 'LSP_PROGRESS' and self.wave_pattern then return wave, else return blocks
code_locations: Init function lines 74-88: Add self.wave_pattern assignment
Provider function lines 134-137: Add conditional check

nodes.description: Create static wave patterns table in NixieProgressBar component
deliverables: Add wave_patterns table to NixieProgressBar.static
9 pattern strings with verified Unicode characters
Comment explaining pattern progression
validation_criteria: Table is in static scope for performance (no recomputation)
Each pattern is exactly 8 characters
Patterns use ⎯ and ⎺ characters correctly
Code follows existing formatting style

nodes.description: Modify LSP detection logic to calculate wave frame and store pattern
deliverables: Add frame calculation in LSP_PROGRESS branch (lines 74-88)
Store frame index and wave pattern in self.wave_pattern
Preserve existing self.state, self.color, self.label assignments
Add inline comment explaining 150ms timing
validation_criteria: Frame calculation: math.floor((vim.loop.now() or 0) / 150) % 9
self.wave_pattern = self.wave_patterns[frame]
No changes to other state variables
Code compiles without errors

metadata.existing_code: local time = (vim.loop.now() or 0) / 200; local frame = math.floor(time) % 9; self.segments = frame + 1
metadata.new_code: local frame = math.floor((vim.loop.now() or 0) / 150) % 9; self.wave_pattern = self.wave_patterns[frame]

nodes.description: Update provider function to use wave pattern for LSP_PROGRESS state
deliverables: Add conditional check for LSP_PROGRESS with wave_pattern
Return wave display: '┣' .. self.wave_pattern .. '┫' .. self.label .. ' '
Preserve existing block-based display for other states
Ensure no breaking changes to provider signature
validation_criteria: Conditional: if self.state == 'LSP_PROGRESS' and self.wave_pattern then
Wave display preserves brackets ┣┫ and ' LSP' label
Other states still use filled/empty block logic
Provider function remains pure (no side effects)

metadata.existing_logic: local filled = string.rep('▓', self.segments); local empty = string.rep('░', 9 - self.segments); return '┣' .. filled .. empty .. '┫' .. self.label .. ' '
metadata.new_logic: if self.state == 'LSP_PROGRESS' and self.wave_pattern then return '┣' .. self.wave_pattern .. '┫' .. self.label .. ' ' end; -- else existing logic
